SASRec scales input embeddings by √d, applies causal attention and padding masks, then normalizes final features before item-dot-product scoring ([original implementation](https://github.com/kang205/SASRec/blob/master/model.py)). For a five-item recency branch, use m_t = Σ[j=0..4] λ^j v_(t−j)e_(t−j) / max(Σ[j=0..4] λ^j v_(t−j), ε), where v marks valid items and 0<λ≤1. Include only positions ≤t; never wrap shifted tensors or include training targets. Mask padding explicitly, return zero for empty windows, and remask after normalization. Proposed scale control: apply branch-only LayerNorm to m_t, matching the approximate coordinate scale of normalized SASRec features h_t. Averaging alone does not preserve variance; avoid adding another normalization to the baseline path when exact initial predictions matter.

For exact initial preservation, use h′=h+W·LN(m), initializing W and its bias to zero; alternatively use h′=h+αP·LN(m), with α=0 and P nonzero-initialized. Zero scalar residual gating follows [ReZero](https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.04887). Do not zero both α and P: that blocks their initial gradients. Convex fusion h′=(1−g)h+g·LN(m), g=sigmoid(b), starts at a 50/50 mixture when b=0; a negative bias gives approximate preservation, never exact for finite b. Convex mixing also does not guarantee unchanged variance.

Prioritize a cheap last-item ablation, h′=h+α·LN(e_t), α=0, with identical masking and scoring. This recommendation is an architectural inference: it isolates immediate-item signal before adding decay and pooling complexity. Compare both using the same macro validation HR@10; neither guarantees improvement.
